senses.gloss: m. (b. h.; = מאחר; אָחַר) next day, future day. Mekh. Bo. 18 יש מ׳ עכשיו וכ׳ there is a maḥar which means now (the next day), and there is a maḥar which means some future time; Yalk. Ex. 225.—
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 28a:12">Ber. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>למ׳ אני ואתה וכ׳</he> to-morrow I and you &c.
<cite ref="Sotah 48b:19">Sot. 48ᵇ</cite> <he>כל מי … מה אוכל למ׳ וכ׳</he> he who has bread in his basket and says, what shall I have to eat to-morrow? &c.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 2:1:7">Y. Gitt. II, 44ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>הוא לילה הוא למ׳ וכ׳</he> it makes no difference whether the same night or the next day or after some time; a. fr.—<cite ref="M00942"><he>מָחֳרָת</he></cite> f., constr. <cite ref="M00942"><he>מָחֲרַת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Menachot 65b:5">Men. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>ממ׳ השבת מ׳ יו״ט</he> ‘the morrow of the Sabbath’ (<cite ref="Leviticus 23:11">Lev. XXIII, 11</cite>) means the day after the first day of the Festival (Passover).
Ib. או אינו אלא למ׳ שבת בראשית may it not mean the morrow after the regular weekly Sabbath?; a. e.—מָחֳרָתַיִם day after to-morrow.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 12">Midr. Till. to Ps. XII</cite> <he>ולמ׳ נלך וכ׳</he> and the day after to-morrow we shall go &c.
